set.approach: The Salal Creek forest road, a branch off the Upper Lillooet road north of Pemberton, ends below the Salal Creek walls (forest road conditions vary, so check before driving). From the road end, walk into the forest aiming a little south of the big slide path that drops from the walls, which keeps you out of thick slide alder. When the slope steepens abruptly, drop left and cross through a gap in the brush onto open ground in the slide path, then go up it to the bivy sites below the walls. The approach is short but steep, and an ice axe, sometimes crampons, are needed on the snow early in the season. The Fantastic Wall is a broad slab cut by a sickle-shaped gully, on the Buttress's left side. Moonraker climbs left of the sickle-shaped feature; the wall is easy to find from the bivy.
set.descent_text: The route ends at a V-notch in the summit ridge. Descend the major couloir between the Fantastic Wall and the Randy Stoltmann Buttress back to the bivy site. It holds snow early in the season, so carry an ice axe and crampons.

review.notes: MP route page: finish at a V-notch in the summit ridge, descent by couloir with axe; area page: approach. Alpine Baking confirms a short steep approach to the bivy and descent via couloirs.

review.notes: MP route page for start and descent; area page and Alpine Baking for approach.

Standing Wave is the leftmost route on the wall and starts at the toe of an arete just left of the major gully that lies left of Moonraker.
set.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit rim after crossing the snowpatch high on the face. Descend the major couloir between the Fantastic Wall and the Randy Stoltmann Buttress back to the bivy site. It holds snow early in the season, so carry an ice axe and crampons. Another option from the rim is the glacier descent, but that slope can shed large blocks in the afternoon.

review.notes: MP route page: start and descent gully; Alpine Baking and Keep Your Heid page: glacier alternative.

set.descent_text: The route joins the ridge shared with Standing Wave and finishes at the summit. From there the plateau leads to the descent glacier; the couloir between the Fantastic Wall and the Randy Stoltmann Buttress is the alternative. Carry an ice axe and crampons.

review.notes: MP page: summit then descend via plateau to descent glacier; standing wave page: gully descent; Alpine Baking: both descents exist.

set.approach: The Salal Creek forest road, a branch off the Upper Lillooet road north of Pemberton, ends below the Salal Creek walls (forest road conditions vary, so check before driving). From the road end, walk into the forest aiming a little south of the big slide path that drops from the walls, which keeps you out of thick slide alder. When the slope steepens abruptly, drop left and cross through a gap in the brush onto open ground in the slide path, then go up it to the bivy sites below the walls. The approach is short but steep, and an ice axe, sometimes crampons, are needed on the snow early in the season. Lillarete climbs the middle of the broad west-dropping face below the Gnomon. From the bivy area, cross the snow to the face of the Randy Stoltmann Buttress and start to the left of the prominent chimney that splits the face, beginning with a flake against the wall.
set.descent_text: Lillarete ends on the summit of Randy Stoltmann Tower, where there is usually a two-piton rappel station. Two rappels lead from the summit to a perched slab and then to the notch behind the tower; the angles are awkward and the rock is loose. From the notch you can escape down the couloir behind it, using a mix of rappels and down-climbing on steep snow and ice, or climb one more long, easier pitch to the rim of the summit plateau and descend from there to the left (north) into the major couloir beside the route. An ice axe and crampons are almost always needed, and anchors may need backing up or replacing, so carry rappel webbing and a few pitons. Do not count on old stations.

review.notes: MP route page and Alpine Baking trip report agree: two rappels from the summit, then a couloir or one more pitch; crampons and ice axe.

The approach is short but steep, and an ice axe, sometimes crampons, are needed on the snow early in the season. The approach is shared with the routes on the Randy Stoltmann Buttress. Starting at the foot of Selective Cut, shift right into the narrow couloir that runs between that buttress and the Octopus Beak tower. It is an early-season line that may be mostly dirt by late summer.

review.notes: MP route page; approach only because the descent from the rim is not described.
